subject: Learning restriction ops and export validation
messages:
From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@medcore.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medcore.com
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Learning restriction ops and export validation

Hi Priyom / Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Before we move to legal/procurement, MedCore needs operational confirmation that Redwood will not use our interactions for model improvement (no-training) and a reproducible evidence bundle we can share with our security team. Specifically: 

- A written commitment we can include in the DPA (no training / no derivatives).
- Artifacts showing data handling: transient KV/prefix caching, retention windows, deletion timelines, and how prompt/response logs are excluded from training pipelines.
- Cross-border transfer controls and where encryption keys are held (onshore KMS vs. cloud-managed).
- A sample audit snippet (redacted) demonstrating request-level audit logs for a thirty-day window.

Can you confirm what you can provide, the format (pdf/docx), and an estimated delivery date? Procurement will also attach a set of DPA redlines — please loop in your legal ops if needed.

Best,
Sarah Li
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
MedCore Health
Attachment: N/A
From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@medcore.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, david_kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Learning restriction ops and export validation

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Short version: we can commit to a contractual no-training clause and assemble an "ops proof pack" containing the artifacts you requested. Details below and next steps.

What we will provide (preview):
- Signed no-training clause language for insertion into the DPA (we can accept your redlines or provide ours).
- "redwood-proof-pack.pdf" (attached) with:
  * Architecture diagram showing inference-only serving (separate telemetry pipeline, explicit non-persisting KV cache for ephemeral sessions).
  * Retention policy table (30-day searchable logs by default, configurable).
  * Deletion playbook and SLA for record-level deletion (API + manual escalation path).
  * Sample redacted audit snippet and event IDs.
- Onshore key options: customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) or Redwood-managed keys scoped to US regions; we'll include KMS locality and key rotation notes.
- Export controls: confirmation of SFTP/API export lanes and a migration path for on-prem exports for regulated pilots.

Proposed timeline: initial proof pack and a short ops checklist by end of week (Fri, 11/12). Full evidence bundle (including export-ready audit logs and DPA redline responses) by Tue, 11/16.

Can we schedule a 30-minute walkthrough Thursday to run the security team through the proof pack? I suggest bringing Kimberly (ops) and David (privacy).

Thanks — we'll start assembling the materials and note the procurement redlines when you send them.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-proof-pack.pdf (preview)
From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@medcore.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medcore.com
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 13:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Learning restriction ops and export validation

Thanks, Priyom — that timeline works. Two clarifications before the call: 

1) Please include a clear table mapping: artifact -> verification method -> acceptance criteria (security will accept the pack if the verification path includes either an on-site demo or a signed audit extract).
2) Can you provide the record-level deletion SLA (hours) and confirmation whether deletion requests are propagated to any downstream telemetry consumers?

Procurement will upload their DPA redlines in a moment (expect a DocuSign link or attached doc).

—Sarah
From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@medcore.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: david_kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Ops checklist and verification plan (pre-call)

Hi Sarah / Priyom — following up with the ops-level checklist we'll include in the proof pack. I'm dropping the checklist here so security knows the acceptance gates ahead of the walkthrough.

Operational proof checklist (high level):
- Artifact: Architecture diagram (attached)
  Verification: 30-min walkthrough + ability to inspect docker images or runtime config in a sandbox.
  Acceptance: Security signs off on inference-only runtime separation.

- Artifact: Retention & deletion matrix (attached ops-checklist.xlsx)
  Verification: Trigger deletion on test tenant, provide event id and audit record.
  Acceptance: Deletion event appears in audit within 15 minutes; complete propagation within 72 hours to telemetry consumers.

- Artifact: Audit snippet (redacted)
  Verification: Provide HMAC-signed audit extract and matching request/response IDs.
  Acceptance: Security validates extract hash and confirms fields present (timestamp, request_id, routing).

- Artifact: KMS residency options
  Verification: Provide KMS ARN and region, show policy scoping for onshore key usage.
  Acceptance: Customer-managed KMS or Redwood-managed onshore keys accepted.

Notes / exceptions:
- For pilot/test tenants we can offer SFTP export of raw logs to customer-owned storage rather than API access.
- Some telemetry (platform health metrics) remain aggregated and cannot be tied to request-level content; these are not used for model training.

Attachments: ops-checklist.xlsx (checklist), redwood-proof-pack.pdf (ops diagrams)

I'll be on the call Thursday; proposed time 11:00 AM PT.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Operations, Redwood Inference
Attachment: ops-checklist.xlsx

Thanks Kim — procurement attached our DPA redlines (DPA_redlines_v3.docx) and asked for the following before legal will proceed: 

- Explicit clause language for no-training and no-derivatives with a specific definition of "model improvement".
- Sample signed audit extract for a real tenant (redacted) and SOC 2 readiness evidence (report date and auditor).
- Confirmation that KMS keys can be customer-managed and will remain in the US region.

We can do the call at 11:00 AM PT today.

—Sarah
Attachment: DPA_redlines_v3.docx
From: david_kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@medcore.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Nov 2027 16:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Ops checklist and verification plan (pre-call)

Hi Sarah — quick summary from privacy/engineering on the items procurement flagged. Priyom / Kim — copying the ask list and next actions.

1) Contract language: we will accept a narrow "no-training/no-derivatives" clause. Draft language attached in the evidence bundle; if MedCore prefers to propose wording, legal can run it and we'll track redlines.

2) Audit extract: we will produce a redacted HMAC-signed extract for a recent tenant covering a 30-day window (fields: timestamp, request_id, route, ingress/egress bytes). That extract will be included in a signed zip file with checksum.

3) SOC 2: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II in our US region; the last report date is 2027-06-01. We'll provide the auditor name and a secure viewing link in the evidence bundle.

4) KMS residency: customer-managed KMS is supported (bring-your-own-key). For customer-managed keys we require RBAC on the key and minimal policies we will share. Keys remain in the region selected at onboarding (we will confirm US region in the bundle).

5) Deletion SLA: we propose a 24-hour acknowledgement and 72-hour propagation window to downstream telemetry consumers (as Kim noted). For high-priority on-prem exports we can tighten propagation to 24 hours with a pilot scope.

Next steps / timeline:
- Ops proof pack (redwood-proof-pack.pdf + ops-checklist.xlsx) delivered by EOD today (11/10).
- Full evidence zip (includes HMAC-signed audit extract, SOC link, DPA draft comments) by Tue, 11/16.
- Legal sync: Priyom to schedule a 30-min DPA call after your legal team reviews our draft.

If procurement needs an interim signed confirmation of the no-training clause to unblock the purchase order, legal can provide a conditional exhibit pending final DPA language.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call if you want the privacy/engineering owner present.

David Kim
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
Attachment: evidence-preview.zip (contains proof pack index)
